page.title: Nominal Style and Information Density
page.subtitle_html: Nominal style and information density - C2 formal noun-based phrasing and compact information flow.
page.subtitle_text: C2 formal noun-based phrasing and compact information flow.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Nominal style and information density: compact anchors for turning actions and clauses into precise formal noun phrases.","rules":[{"label":"Nominal focus","text":"Use nouns such as implementation, assessment, expansion, and reduction to make formal claims more compact.","example":"The implementation of this policy will require careful planning."},{"label":"Dense information flow","text":"Pack supporting detail into controlled noun phrases without obscuring the main claim.","example":"The committee's assessment of the evidence was cautious."},{"label":"Formal register","text":"Prefer nominal structures when the style requires distance, precision, or institutional tone.","example":"A gradual reduction in costs is expected."}]}

blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on nominal style and information density.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"C1 Mixed Revision: compact anchor for the final Sentence Builder C1 mixed drill.","rules":[{"label":"Mixed structures","text":"Review advanced conditionals, inversion, passive, reporting, clauses, modal perfect, and formal style together.","example":"If I had accepted the offer, I would be working abroad now."},{"label":"Meaning first","text":"Choose the structure that preserves tense, emphasis, register, and logical relation.","example":"Not only did the policy change, but its effects were also immediate."},{"label":"Final drill","text":"Use the final lesson to test flexible C1 sentence construction across the whole course.","example":"The report is believed to have been revised before publication."}]}

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"C2 mixed revision: compact anchors for the final English Sentence Builder C2 drill across advanced conditionals, cohesion, modality, and formal grammar.","rules":[{"label":"Advanced review","text":"Combine previously learned C2 patterns without changing the intended register or meaning.","example":"Had it not been for his support, the project would have failed."},{"label":"Cohesion and precision","text":"Keep sentence links clear when combining contrast, result, reference, or reformulation.","example":"That said, the conclusion requires stronger evidence."},{"label":"Final accuracy","text":"Check modal meaning, passive style, dense noun phrases, and formal tone in one controlled sentence.","example":"You need not have arrived so early."}]}
